title: Services list flat by date with the schedule as a column
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a service advisor with view customers (and edit customers to add or change a record), on the build under test.
  2. Open an asset page and its Maintenance tab (the last tab, after Notes). The asset card is on the left; the Compliance section sits below Contact.
  3. A unit enrolled on two schedules, with one service overdue for several cycles and one service shared across both schedules. Seed: enrol the unit on two schedules that share a service; set a service overdue by backdating its last-service date.
custom_steps:
1. Read the service list beneath the reading cards: its sort, the schedule column and grouping.
  2. Read one row: next due, the rule beneath, and Last done.
  3. Find the multi-cycle-overdue service and the service shared by two schedules.
  4. Hover the (i) beside the list heading.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Services are listed flat and sorted by date, with the schedule as a column (not grouped by schedule); each row shows next due as a date with the rule beneath, and Last done as the date its cycle counts from (labelled so it is not confused with a line completion date).
  • A service appears once - a unit that missed four cycles shows one row reading overdue with the date it fell due.
  • A unit on two schedules carrying the same service shows two rows, each with its schedule as a chip.
  • On the design the (i) reads "One list for the whole asset, ordered by what comes due first. Schedules are a column, not a heading, so two schedules never split the order."

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10566 (S9, The asset Maintenance tab), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S9 (unchanged requirements); Design board "Chunk 1.dc.html" (MR V2 Claude Design project, version of 6 October 2026), artboard S4; read 6 Oct 2026.
